Exercise 1: Examining the source

x-axis label: longitude
y-axis label: latitude

The colours represent each of the eight populations tracked and the routes they migrated respectively

The map is a Mercator projection and displayed locations are as follows: breeding site (circles), Iberian peninsula stopover (filled downward triangles), westernmost location during autumn migration (open triangles), nonbreeding area (squares), and post-Saharan crossing stopover (filled upward triangles)

Exercise 2: Examining the data

The longitude of Moscow is 36.7 degrees

```{r}
library(gt)
library(tidyverse)
library(maps)

```

Exercise 3: Read the first CSV file

```{r}

bird_breeding_sites <- read.csv("data/breeding_site_locations.csv")

gt(bird_breeding_sites)

```


```{r}
colnames(bird_breeding_sites)


glimpse(bird_breeding_sites)

```

Exercise 5: Using the pipe operator

```{r}

input_vec <- c(5, -10, 4, -3)

mean_vec <- input_vec |> mean() |> abs() |> round()

print(mean_vec)

```

Exercise 6: Select, de-duplicate and rename


```{r}

bird_migration_selected <- migration |> select(Site, winterLongitude, winterLatitude, pslon, pslat, iblon, iblat, awestlon, awestlat) |> distinct() |> rename(Winter_Longitude = winterLongitude, Winter_Latitude = winterLatitude, Stopover_Longitude = pslon, Stopover_Latitude = pslat, Iberian_Longitude = iblon, Iberian_Latitude = iblat, Westmost_Longitude = awestlon, Westmost_Latitude = awestlat)

```
